page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 976.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.25 GB per vCPU. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz and includes a 54 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-threaded and memory-intensive capabilities. The instance achieves a strong rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 293.92 GB/sec and a strong PassMark CPU score of 54,571.25. Geekbench multi-core tests, software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing also fall into the strong tier. However, single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1,852.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,577.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 150.66 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 62.1 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-64 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for large-scale in-memory databases and enterprise applications that require massive RAM footprints without needing proportional scaling of compute cores. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and GPU accelerators, meaning all storage must be network-attached, and workloads requiring hardware acceleration are not supported. The instance is optimized for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise resource planning workloads.
